analysis.requirement: R6 — Spatially resolved smoke exposure: construct hourly spatial PM2.5 exposure surfaces (regulatory monitors, calibrated low-cost sensors, satellite/modeled products, meteorology, indoor shelter PM2.5); estimate reductions in time-weighted exposure attributable to outreach, transportation, capacity, and siting; do not present inhaled dose unless ventilation and infiltration are defensibly measured or bounded.
exists_defensible: Hourly measured PM2.5 for the exact event window: EPA AQS parameter 88502, 4,795 rows, 7 tri-county monitors (2 in Multnomah), 312/312 hourly slices with zero gaps, SHA-256 recorded, reproducible via scripts/fetch-aqs-pm25.ps1; the file retains all 24 EPA columns including per-row monitor Latitude/Longitude (Geography/data/README.md:68-110). The temporal half of R6 is genuinely satisfied.

A reviewer-ready defense of the uniform-field choice: docs/final/SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md states plainly 'we do not interpolate. There is no spatial model' (lines 7-8), explains why 2 in-county monitors cannot support kriging or IDW (lines 64-79), why the specified LOOCV decision test is unexecutable with 2 stations (line 114), and names the consequence — all exposure variation is time outdoors; placement helps only by shortening journeys and its benefit is a lower bound (lines 95-106). Registered as active assumption A-01 (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:79; per evidence inventory, Geography/data/registry/assumptions.csv row A-01).

Manuscript disclosure of the uniformity assumption in three places: Eq. 1 defines C(t) as countywide (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:117-119); the four exposure measures are declared non-independent because the field is uniform (md:210); the limitations carry the two-monitor justification and the consequence that placement can never move people into cleaner air (md:307 per evidence inventory, tex:998-1001). This is a correctly hedged assumption, not a hidden one.

Instrument-bias disclosure with direction: heated-inlet nephelometry volatilizes semi-volatile organics, so readings 'most likely understate true PM2.5 during the event'; Uncertainty column empty in all 4,795 rows; no FRM co-location (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:125-137; md:85). Also EPA's own IT wildfire qualifier spans exactly the simulation window (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:56-60).

Time-weighted exposure attribution to CAPACITY and SITING exists under the uniform field: A-to-B exposure falls 87.3% (md:208-210); B-to-C a further 50.7% with dose 3,056-to-1,536 ug (md:236); the random-pool control demotes siting's headcount credit to dispersion, leaving siting credit on walking distance only (md:238); window arms W24/W72 decompose walking's share of the dose benefit over observation horizon (evidence inventory: docs/runs/phaseD-windows, docs/final/TECHNICAL_REFERENCE.md:2207-2211). These attributions are internally rigorous but are time-outdoors attributions, not spatial-exposure attributions.

Dose restraint partially exists: susceptibility weights were set to 1.0 after the cited RRs failed audit, with a full category-error account (md:170-176) — exemplary discipline exactly in R6's spirit. The exposure integral was independently recomputed from the raw EPA file (54,002.7 vs 54,002.8, md:198; recomputation itself REPORTED, not re-executed by this audit).

Caveat on the audit doc itself: SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md is dated 2026-07-26 at commit 02c3181 and its section-4 placement-benefit figures (-5.65% exposure, -12.57% dose) are from an older run family than the manuscript's present-day arms (further 50.7% B-to-C, md:236) — its reasoning is current, its example numbers are stale.
missing: ABSENT: any spatial variation in PM2.5. One scalar per hour county-wide; 'a resident in St. Johns and a resident in Lents receive identical concentrations at every tick' (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:18-30). No exposure surface of any kind exists.

ABSENT: low-cost sensor data. '2020 PurpleAir coverage for Portland was not acquired' — recorded as future work (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:116). Repo grep for PurpleAir hits only discussion documents, no data files.

ABSENT: satellite or modeled smoke products (NOAA HMS plumes, AOD, HRRR-Smoke, CMAQ/Downscaler). Grep hits only the audit's why-not table (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:117) and DATA_SOURCES.md discussion; no product files in repo.

ABSENT: meteorology of any kind. The D4 meteorology item was deliberately deferred (evidence inventory: docs/science/DATA_SOURCES.md:140-162); no wind/mixing-height/temperature data exists in the repo.

ABSENT: indoor shelter PM2.5 measurements and any infiltration model. 'the model does not simulate indoor air at all — the study endpoint is arrival at the door' (docs/final/PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md:16-20). The words infiltration/indoor air/indoor PM appear NOWHERE in docs/chapter (grep verified) — the manuscript never discloses this boundary.

ABSENT: exposure reduction attributable to TRANSPORTATION — no transport mechanism of any kind exists in the model (evidence inventory: grep of Geography/src found no bus/vehicle/ride code path; walking is the only mode). The attribution R6 asks for is structurally impossible for this lever.

ABSENT: exposure reduction attributable to OUTREACH grounded in data — the outreach conversion rate lambdaOutreachPerDay is declared UNSOURCED ('a real outreach-contact rate for this event does not exist in the record', evidence inventory: registry V41/A-31); swept 0-0.2/day but any exposure attribution from it is assumption-on-assumption.

ABSENT: defensible ventilation bound for inhaled dose. The resting rate 0.61 m3/h is not in the cited EPA source, and the recorded sensitivity sweep 0.4-0.8 m3/h excludes the source's own Sedentary cells 0.25-0.30 entirely, so the existing bound fails to bracket (docs/science/D16-EFH-VENTILATION-DEFECT.md:97,105-107). D16's own verdict: 'do not publish V25 as currently sourced' (D16:132).
implementable_with_existing_data: Inter-monitor spread bound (buildable now): Geography/data/airnow/aqs_hourly_pm25_portland_2020-09.csv carries per-row monitor coordinates and per-hour values for both in-county sites (0080, 2011) plus 5 tri-county sites (Geography/data/README.md:84-110). Compute the hourly two-monitor disagreement |C_0080 - C_2011| and tri-county range across all 312 hours, and publish it as an empirical uncertainty envelope on every exposure figure — this converts 'we cannot resolve gradients' into 'unresolved spatial heterogeneity is bounded by X ug/m3 at the monitors'. The peak split (562.7 mean vs 588.9 single-monitor, SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:45-54) shows the band is nontrivial but computable.

Monitor-swap sensitivity (buildable now, one model-run campaign): rerun A/B/C with the field set to site 0080 only and site 2011 only. Because departure gating uses C(t) >= 55.5, this tests whether the behavioral cascade, not just the integral, is robust to the choice of station. Data already in repo; no new acquisition.

Post-arrival exposure under bounded infiltration (buildable from archives): arrival times are in the archived agents.csv (first-hour survival analysis was computed from B-seed42 agents.csv per evidence inventory, docs/PRESENTATION_PROVENANCE.md:55), and the hourly series is in the AQS CSV. Recompute sheltered-time exposure under literature infiltration factors Fin in a stated bracket instead of the current implicit Fin=0, and report scenario exposure reductions as a range. This directly repairs the largest R6 overreach without a single new observation.

Widened ventilation-rate sensitivity per D16's own prescription: widen the resting IR sweep to 0.25-0.80 m3/h so it spans the EPA table's candidate cells, and restate dose as ratio-dependent (2.25x-5.40x band, D16-EFH-VENTILATION-DEFECT.md:95-107,116-120). Parameter exists in the model; requires re-runs, not new data.

Reframing pass (buildable now, zero computation): SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:100-103 already supplies the correct language — exposure contrasts are 'an access/duration statistic wearing exposure units'. Porting that sentence and the arrival-at-the-door endpoint disclosure into the manuscript (currently absent, grep-verified) is a text-only fix.

Tri-county LOOCV demonstration: with 7 stations in the existing CSV, a leave-one-out comparison of uniform-mean vs IDW prediction at each held-out station is computable and would document quantitatively (not just argumentatively) that interpolation adds error, strengthening the A-01 defense. The audit notes the 5 outer monitors 'remain available for a future cross-validation' (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:81-87).
needs_new_empirical_data: Indoor PM2.5 in shelter facilities: deploy paired indoor/outdoor calibrated low-cost monitors (with pre/post co-location against a DEQ station) in a sample of the 36 facilities during a future smoke episode — the only way to ever ground an infiltration factor or the retracted 'clean-air-capable' label.

Facility filtration/air-exchange survey: structured survey or site audit of the shelter inventory (HVAC type, filter MERV rating, portable air cleaner presence), optionally CO2-decay air-exchange measurements — cheap, and sufficient to bound infiltration by facility class even without an event.

Population time-activity/ventilation observation would be needed only if absolute inhaled-dose magnitudes are retained as headline results; otherwise the D16 bounded-sensitivity route makes this unnecessary.
needs_external_acquisition: PurpleAir historical archive, Portland metro, Sept 2020 (candidate source: PurpleAir historical data API). The repo's own audit names this the one 'possibly feasible' path to a real surface (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:116); requires EPA wildfire-smoke correction (Barkjohn-type) whose validity under dense wood smoke the audit itself flags as contested.
Oregon DEQ non-AQS continuous or temporary monitors for the 2020 event, if any beyond the two AQS sites existed (candidate source: Oregon DEQ Air Quality program data requests).
NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke plume polygons for Sept 2020 (candidate source: NOAA OSPO HMS archive) — coarse binary plume masks usable as a fusion covariate, not a surface by themselves.
Meteorology: hourly ASOS/METAR from PDX/Troutdale/Hillsboro (candidate source: NOAA ISD / Iowa Environmental Mesonet) — required covariates for any defensible fusion model; none in repo.

Modeled surfaces: HRRR-Smoke experimental output for Sept 2020 (candidate source: NOAA GSL archives; 2020 availability uncertain — experimental product then) and EPA fused CMAQ/Downscaler daily surfaces (candidate source: EPA RSIG). Satellite AOD downscaling was assessed in-repo as 'not feasible here' for this event due to heavy smoke/cloud confusion (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:117) — any acquisition should treat AOD as supporting, not primary.
JOHS/Multnomah County records on any 2020 indoor air measures at OCC/Charles Jordan (candidate source: county public-records request) — existence unverified; the repo holds no such record.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'All 36 clean-air-capable facilities' — the manuscript twice asserts the facilities are clean-air-capable
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:97 and :182 (and per evidence inventory tex:315, tex:582)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The project's own results doc retracts the wording: 'That was an overstatement... Nothing in the sources establishes that these buildings filter their air, and the model does not simulate indoor air at all' (docs/final/PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md:16-20). Under R6 this is a claim about indoor exposure quality supported by zero indoor measurements and no infiltration model; the retraction exists but never reached the manuscript.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Inhaled-dose magnitudes presented as results — Eq. 4 with IR = 1.62/0.61 m3/h 'from the EPA Exposure Factors Handbook', and 'mean inhaled dose from 3,056 to 1,536 ug'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: R6 explicitly says avoid inhaled dose unless ventilation rates are defensibly measured or bounded. The 0.61 resting rate is not in the cited source (D16-EFH-VENTILATION-DEFECT.md:97: 'not in the source'), the published 2.7x walk:rest ratio could be 2.25x-5.40x depending on the true cell (D16:95-99), and the recorded sensitivity sweep 0.4-0.8 excludes the source's Sedentary cells, so the existing bound demonstrably fails to bracket (D16:105-107). D16's standing instruction: 'do not publish V25 as currently sourced' (D16:132).

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Cross-scenario exposure reductions (87.3% A-to-B, 93.7% C vs A) implicitly assume indoor concentration = 0 after admission, and the manuscript never discloses this
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:170 ('Accumulation stops when a resident is admitted') together with :208 and :236; grep of docs/chapter finds zero occurrences of 'infiltration', 'indoor air', or an endpoint disclosure
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Sheltered time is booked at zero exposure — an unstated infiltration-factor-of-zero assumption. Wildfire-smoke infiltration into unfiltered buildings is substantial, so absolute reduction magnitudes are overstated by an unquantified amount (direction survives). The disclosure exists only in a results doc (PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md:18-19), not in either manuscript form.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Exposure-unit headline sentences without in-sentence uniform-field conditioning — e.g. 'reduces total modeled exposure by 93.7%, person-hours above threshold by 93.6%'
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:236; abstract-level exposure claims per evidence inventory md:27
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The repo's own audit states that with a uniform field every such statistic 'is an access/duration statistic wearing exposure units' and exposure inequality 'is not environmental inequality' (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:100-103). The manuscript's md:210 caution covers co-movement of the four measures but the audit's sharper reframe never appears in the chapter, so exposure-unit sentences read as environmental-exposure findings that the data cannot support spatially. This is the mildest of the four — the hedge exists nearby — but an ERL reviewer will enforce the audit's own sentence.

proposed_methods: Data fusion surface (full R6 closure): acquire 2020 Portland PurpleAir + DEQ/AQS anchors + ASOS meteorology; apply EPA wildfire correction to low-cost sensors; fit hourly surfaces by regression kriging or universal kriging (HMS plume mask and wind as covariates); validate by leave-one-out at the two AQS sites and across sensors; then re-run the model with C(x,t) sampled at agent positions and integrate exposure along Dijkstra polylines (per-tick positions already exist), which for the first time lets siting move people into cleaner air — the channel currently zero by construction (md:307).

Bounding fallback (defensible without acquisition): publish the hourly inter-monitor disagreement band from the existing 7-monitor CSV as the spatial-uncertainty envelope on all exposure figures; add monitor-swap sensitivity runs (field = site 0080 only vs 2011 only) to show behavioral robustness; add the computable tri-county LOOCV to convert the anti-interpolation argument into a measurement.

Indoor term: replace the implicit Fin=0 with a two-compartment mass-balance using literature wildfire infiltration factors as labeled scenario bounds; recompute sheltered-time exposure from archived arrival times + the hourly series; report scenario contrasts as ranges; delete or condition 'clean-air-capable' per the existing retraction text.

Dose repair per D16's own checklist: choose the EFH activity cell that matches modeled waiting behavior, widen the resting-IR sweep to 0.25-0.80 m3/h, restate every dose figure and the walk:rest ratio as ratio-dependent — or demote inhaled dose to a supplementary sensitivity and lead with the concentration-time integral, which R6 permits.

Attribution accounting: report time-weighted exposure deltas per lever explicitly — capacity (A-to-B), siting (B-to-C with the random-pool control already in hand), outreach (lambda sweep, labeled assumption-driven), and state that transportation attribution is impossible in the current model because no transport mechanism exists; with any spatial surface, decompose each delta into a time-outdoors component and a concentration-differential component.

Manuscript reframing (zero-cost, do regardless): port SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md section 4's language and the arrival-at-the-door endpoint disclosure into the chapter, retitle exposure results as time-outdoors metrics where the field is uniform, and keep 562.7 labeled as the two-monitor mean with the understatement caveat already at md:85.
analysis.priority_rationale: For ERL this is the requirement the venue is named for, and it splits the project cleanly in two. The headline findings — 30.1%/91.6%/96.0% access, 550 refusals at one-space-per-person, the dispersion-not-optimizer attribution, the mobility equity gap — are access results that do not depend on spatial smoke at all and would survive R6 enforcement intact with reframing. What does not survive as currently written is the paper's environmental-science layer: by the repo's own audit every exposure statistic is 'an access/duration statistic wearing exposure units' (SMOKE_FIELD_AUDIT.md:100-103), the inhaled-dose magnitudes rest on a ventilation constant absent from its cited source with a sweep that fails to bracket the source's own cells (D16, standing instruction 'do not publish V25 as currently sourced'), the manuscript still calls facilities 'clean-air-capable' against its own retraction, and sheltered time is silently booked at zero exposure with no infiltration disclosure anywhere in the chapter. The mitigating facts are real: the two-in-county-monitor constraint is genuine, the uniformity assumption is honestly registered (A-01) and disclosed three times in the manuscript, and the audit document is close to reviewer-proof on why interpolation was refused. Priority is therefore two-tier. Tier 1 (blocking for any submission, cheap, fully implementable now): the reframing pass, the indoor-endpoint disclosure, the clean-air-capable deletion, the D16 dose repair or demotion, and the inter-monitor bounding band — these convert honest-but-scattered caveats into manuscript text and remove every claim R6 can reject outright. Tier 2 (scope decision): actual surface construction via PurpleAir fusion is a moderate acquisition-plus-methods project that would upgrade the paper from an access study wearing exposure units into a genuine exposure study, unlock the moving-people-into-cleaner-air channel for siting, and is the single change most likely to move an ERL editor from reject-as-out-of-scope to review; but the paper can be submitted defensibly without it if Tier 1 is done and the framing leads with access, not exposure.
